To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Hebrew Bible contains oracles about the future that are not based on the knowledge of the future but are rather based on a belief in God's power over the future, and that these oracles were uttered in a ritual context.

The Hebrew oracles are not primarily political; they are not uttered in war; they are not the work of individual prophets/seers; they are not regarded as mad; they are not unsolicited; they are not part of the Greek mantei; and they are not uttered by individuals.

the Hebrew Bible contains a large number of oracles against foreign nations, that the oracles are not all of the same type, and that the majority of the oracles are found in the prophets, with the exception of Isaiah 13-14, 34-35, and Jeremiah 50-51, where the oracles are part and parcel of the book.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the oracular speeches of the prophets are related to the cult.
the following questions: (1) What is the nature and structure of the oracles about nations?
the following: (1) the oracular speech in the Greek world; (2) the oracular speeches in the Hebrew Bible; (3) a comparison between the oracular speech of both traditions; (4) a conclusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hebrew oracles about the nation are not manteia.
the oracles of the Hebrew Bible are very different from the Greek oracles.
the Greek oracles are not like the Hebrew oracles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oracles in the Hebrew Bible do not belong to a genre which is similar to the Greek oracle.
the Hebrew oracles about the nation were uttered in a cultic context, were liturgical, and were part of a structured and ordered collection of texts.
Hagedorn’s thesis is not valid, and the Hebrew oracles should be regarded as a part of the liturgy of the temple, not a part of the history of the nation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hebrew oracles about the nation are a literary genre, and that they have a long history of composition.
the Hebrew oracles have to be understood in their own context and not by comparison with the Greek manteis.
the Hebrew oracles about the other nations are part of the worship of YHWH, the God of Israel.
